idiom_name: Core Data NSFetchRequest + NSPredicate (also Fluent, GRDB)
implementation_notes: Core Data's NSFetchRequest is the pattern's definition in code: it collects the entity (NSEntityDescription or entity name), an NSPredicate constraining which properties match, NSSortDescriptors, fetchLimit/fetchOffset and the result type, can be stored in the model as a named template with variable placeholders, and is executed against an NSManagedObjectContext. What replaces the classic query class is the framework's request object - and in server-side Swift, Fluent's QueryBuilder or GRDB's QueryInterface; a hand-written request builder stays justified only where several entities must be queried uniformly.
pitfalls: NSPredicate(format:) is stringly typed: a typo or interpolated user input crashes at runtime - format constants are substituted, never sanitised.
A fetch request belongs to one NSManagedObjectContext: executing or reusing it across contexts and queues violates Core Data's concurrency rules.
Fetching more than needed (no fetchLimit, propertiesToFetch or returnsObjectsAsFaults) is the documented mistake that turns a small query object into a performance problem.
